findings: Disabled items remain focusable and cannot activate, following current M3/APG guidance. Material Web navigation source skips them, so its behavior is not copied unchanged.
Native semantic item actions, serializable house events, shared overlay lifetime/placement and TanStack state remain the selected boundaries.
Nested menu scope must exclude descendant menu items. Tab leaves menus; Escape closes the topmost owner and returns focus.
Checkbox/radio menu items require actual checked semantics; checkmark-only Pro examples are insufficient.
Material Web own timers/state/animation engine and DOM-bearing event payloads are reference behavior, not adopted infrastructure.
implementationFollowup: Disabled discovery follows APG/Material guidance, not the Lit implementation skip-disabled behavior.
CSS focus-within is not a reliable parent-ownership oracle for nested native popovers; composed slots/shadow ancestry is used.
Label and description use the existing semantic controller defaults so native element references are retained.
